www.vekn.net/event-calendar/event/9152

Enchant Kindred (German Nationals 2019)
Bad Nauheim, Germany
3 rounds + finals
18 players
Winner: Ralf "extrala" Lammert

*

Top 5 players after 3 rounds were:

Ralf "extrala" Lammert (GER), 2 gw + 9.5 vp, Lasombra g45 Stealth Bleed with Nocturns
Marius Iscru (FRA), 2 gw + 7 vp, Toreador g12 Cel Gun with Ashurs
Sascha Müller (GER), 1 gw + 4.5 vp, Tzimisce g23 with War Ghouls
Joscha Duell (GER), 1 gw + 4 vp, Ventrue g23 Stealth Vote and Bleed
Markus Hißnauer (GER), 1 gw + 3.5 vp, Toreador antitribu g23 Palla Grande Bleed

Final's seating:
Markus > Marius > Joscha > Ralf > Sascha

Finals had 2 h 15 min playing time.
1st oust after 1 hour: Sascha => 1 vp for Ralf
2nd oust after 1 hour 20 minutes: Markus => 2 vp for Ralf
3rd oust after 1 hour 25 minutes: Ralf => 1 vp for Joscha
4th oust after 1 hour 30 minutes: Joscha => 2 vp for Marius
=> Ralf new German Champion due to better seating and winner of the artwork "Enchant Kindred"

Messages.Author: extrala
Messages.Body:
> Mewcat wrote:
> What is marius's motivation in the 2 man finals end game within the context f play to win? I imagine there is sort of an unwritten rule that he should not transfer out at that point but there is absolutely nothing to gain for him.
>
You're absolutely right, Marius had no more incentive to win, after Joscha had ousted me. He could have thrown the game either to me or to Joscha at that point in time. But he was clearly in better position than Joscha then, and he proved sportsmanship by playing on imho.

So kudos to Marius, he also had actually the strongest game & deck in the final round.

Btw, I wouldn't mind a change of rules, that in case of this kind of tie, the last man standing man wins, instead of resolving the tie by preliminary rounds standings,

Messages.Author: Mewcat
Messages.Body: How did he prove sportmanship? His options are to win for one of 2 people that are not himself. If we are to assume this is a competitive endeavor the point for him is to win, not lose in style.

Messages.Author: angrynewb
Messages.Body:
Back in the old days there was actually this rule. Last man standing would win in case of a tie.

While Marius wasnt bound to play to win rule in the final (in final its play to win tournament instead), he could still play for ranking points. 2 VP = 8 Ranking points in the World Ranking

Messages.Body:
> Mewcat wrote:
> How did he prove sportmanship? His options are to win for one of 2 people that are not himself. If we are to assume this is a competitive endeavor the point for him is to win, not lose in style.
>
So what have you done in his place? Simply die so that I become the champion? Just sit there doing nothing until time out to let extrala take the win? I'm curious.

Marius played on to get the best result he could. I would have done the same in his shoes. You don't?

By the way I played rubbish (with hindsight) in ousting extrala. I should have wait until extrala and Marius had weaken each other enough to have a chance of the GW. But I was tired and didn't realize clearly enough, that Marius had to rush extralas vampires to don't get bled and I could cycle in the meantime for Banishments to get rid of the dangerous but bloodless gunslingers and get rid of the Haven Uncovereds on my vampires. So I was just a sitting duck for Marius' vamps.

Baron of Frankfurt

Messages.Author: Mewcat
Messages.Body: What would I have done? Realized that I have no competitive motivation to play and then made a choice based on whatever benefited me as a person, such as if hungry transfer out and go eat, if my friend was finishing a pick up game finish the game out and most likely get 2 vp. This is called rational action, where the things I do are done to benefit me in some way.

Messages.Author: kschaefer
Messages.Body:
> Tournament wrote:
>
> ...For tournaments, playing to win means playing to get a Game Win if it is reasonably possible, and when a Game Win is not reasonably possible, then playing to get as many Victory Points as possible....
>
> During the finals, playing to win means playing to finish as tournament winner (as defined in 3.7.5).
>
The problem with the "[d]uring the finals" line is that is doesn't default to the previous "get as many Victory Points as possible" when you cannot win. I think the PtW rule for the finals should do so, encouraging the remaining players to do as well as they can.
